name: Pulsegrid
positioning: Bottom-up. Free tier is genuinely usable; monetizes on volume, not seats.

pages.title: Pulsegrid — Pricing
pages.text: Pulsegrid charges per event ingested, not per seat. Seats are unlimited on every plan including Free. The Free tier includes 1M events per month with full feature access and 14-day retention. Paid plans start at $49/month for 5M events and extend retention to 12 months. There is no annual commitment and no overage penalty — ingestion above your plan is billed at the same per-event rate. Self-hosting is available under a source-available license at no license cost.

pages.title: Pulsegrid Docs — Quickstart
pages.text: Drop in the Pulsegrid snippet and events flow immediately; identify() is optional and anonymous sessions are stitched retroactively when a user later identifies. The web SDK is 9kb gzipped. Server-side ingestion is available on all plans including Free.

pages.title: Pulsegrid Docs — Limits
pages.text: Ingestion accepts 500 events per second per project on paid plans, 100 on Free. Warehouse sync is not offered; Pulsegrid instead exposes a read-only Postgres endpoint you can query directly. There is no SSO on Free or Starter — SAML lands on the $499 Scale plan. Audit logging is not currently available on any plan.

reviews.quote: The free tier is not a demo, it's a product. We ran production on it for five months before paying. Per-event pricing meant our bill scaled with usage instead of headcount.
Great DX, thin on governance. No audit logs and SSO only at $499 was a hard stop for our security review.
Pulsegrid is the one I'd pick for a new project. Ask me again when legal gets involved.
